# RecreationPrompt.md

Create a mobile-first canvas tower-defense game called **Sky-Pipe Aviary Defense**. It should feel visually inspired by Flappy Bird’s bright sky, pipes, birds, and arcade simplicity, but it must play as a lane-defense strategy game rather than as a flap-physics runner.

Use a 5-row by 7-column battlefield. The player selects a defender card and taps an open grid cell to place it. The player taps falling resource orbs to collect currency. Enemy invaders enter from the right and move left along fixed lanes. If an invader crosses the left defense edge, the player loses. Defender cards have costs and cooldowns. Include ranged seed shooters, resource-producing birds, nest/wall blockers, egg-bomb instant damage, and an elite melee wing guardian that destroys standard enemies quickly and damages bosses heavily. Include solo wave defense and a local two-player versus mode where the second player spends a separate enemy currency to send invaders into lanes.

The presentation should be procedural and readable: no stock-background dependence. Draw bird defenders, pipe goblins, fast crows, helmet crawlers, and a giant pipe-machine boss with Canvas/SVG/CSS shapes. Build animated backgrounds with parallax clouds, vertical pipe towers, feather particles, sky gradients, lane wind streaks, and HUD chrome that resembles an aviary flight console. The five-level progression should move through: Sunrise Training Perch, Cloudgap Pipe Run, Neon Duct Migration, Storm Roost Siege, and Citadel of the Giant Pipe. Each level should remain mechanically compatible with the same tower-defense loop while the world identity, color, atmosphere, and safe pressure cues evolve.

Keep controls large and mobile-safe. Preserve pause, resume, restart, menu, mission brief, boss victory, and breach-loss states. Do not add actual Flappy Bird one-tap flap movement, do not remove lane placement, and do not rewrite the physics/collision loop.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint.md — Remix v4 Inference Plus

## Current game reality

### High-level code structure
- `index.html` is a single-file HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game.
- CSS defines a mobile-first full-screen layout, menu screens, HUD bars, card UI, safe-area padding, button styles, and reaction GIF overlays.
- JavaScript defines static `PLANTS` and `ZOMBIES` data tables, a procedural Canvas `Renderer`, and a `Game` class that owns state, input, update loop, rendering, UI, audio, and screen transitions.

### Game loop / state model
- Main state values observed: `MENU`, `PLAY`, `PAUSE`, `GAMEOVER`.
- `requestAnimationFrame` drives `loop(t)`.
- During `PLAY`, `update(dt)` advances economy, wave spawning, cooldowns, unit attacks, zombie movement/collisions, projectiles, particles, and resource drops; `render()` redraws the lane battlefield.
- Start menu offers Solo Defense, Local 2P Versus, and Mission Brief.
- Pause and end screens are modal overlays.

### Player goals
- Solo: protect the left-side defense line by deploying defenders into a 5x7 lane grid and defeating incoming zombies. Defeating the solo boss displays `SECTOR SECURED!` and returns to menu.
- Versus: Player 1 deploys defenders; Player 2 spends brain currency to spawn zombies into rows.

### Interaction pattern
- Tap/select a card, then tap a grid cell or lane.
- Tap suns to collect currency.
- Use DOM buttons for start, info, pause, resume, restart, and menu.

### Core systems
- Grid placement and occupancy.
- Sun/brain currency economy.
- Card costs and cooldowns.
- Solo wave timer with increasing spawn pressure.
- Enemy lane movement, plant blocking/eating, projectile hits, instant bomb damage, executioner melee takedowns.
- Canvas-only procedural unit rendering.
- Approved remote catalog audio/GIF/font usage already present.

### Inferred genre/gameplay shape
The implemented game is a lane-based tower-defense / wave-defense arcade strategy game inspired by Plants vs. Zombies, not an endless flapping game.

### Current identity summary
The current presentation is **Garden Defenders: Executioner Update**: dark garden defense with zombies, plants, an executioner defender, ember/red UI styling, reaction GIF overlays, and action-loop audio.

## Intended remixed trajectory from prompt: `flappy bird`

The remix should not convert the game into a Flappy Bird clone because that would break protected mechanics. Downstream stages should reinterpret the current tower-defense battlefield as **Sky-Pipe Aviary Defense**:
- lanes become sky corridors between vertical pipe towers;
- defenders become perched bird guardians, seed launchers, nest shields, egg-bombs, and an elite winged executioner/eagle guardian;
- zombies become pipe goblins, smog birds, helmeted pipe crawlers, fast darting crows, and a giant pipe-machine boss;
- sun currency can be visually reframed as feathers, glow seeds, or wing-energy while preserving the existing `sun` economy semantics;
- brain currency in versus can be visually reframed as pipe pressure or flock panic while preserving the existing `brains` economy semantics.

## Preserve-vs-change guidance

### Preserve
- 5 rows x 7 columns grid geometry.
- Tap-card-then-tap-grid placement semantics.
- Tap-to-collect resource semantics.
- Solo wave spawning and increasing pressure.
- Versus two-sided card spawning semantics.
- Plant/zombie stats, costs, cooldowns, attacks, collision rules, movement direction, lose condition, boss victory sequence, pause/restart/menu flow.
- Canvas render/update architecture and `requestAnimationFrame` loop.

### Change safely
- Names, menu copy, HUD labels, button copy.
- Procedural unit silhouettes, colors, motifs, and background layers.
- CSS theme palette, typography, UI chrome, safe decorative animations.
- Level/world planning metadata.
- Audio mapping only through approved catalog sources and without blocking play if media fails.
- Cosmetic particles and non-colliding environmental motion.

### Avoid
- Adding a one-button flap control.
- Replacing lanes with vertical pipe-gap traversal.
- Rewriting collision, projectile, placement, spawn, or economy logic.
- Changing win/loss semantics.
- Creating derived level files in this inference-only stage unless a later level-adapter stage explicitly requests them.
